evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with suspected or confirmed tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in India: when to suspect it, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and imaging work-up, anti-tubercular therapy (ATT), corticosteroids and complications. Built on the ICMR Adult Tubercular Meningitis workflow (March 2022) and the ICMR drug-sensitive TB treatment workflow as per the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) (March 2022).
findings: Suspicion criteria, risk factors, examination, imaging-before-lumbar-puncture rule, laboratory and CSF tests, CSF patterns by meningitis type, NAAT caveat, ATT phases and duration, dexamethasone and prednisolone regimens, complications and follow-up checked against the ICMR Adult TBM STW (March 2022).
Weight-band fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablets, mg/kg doses, streptomycin use in TBM and pyridoxine 10 mg checked against the ICMR NTEP drug-sensitive TB STW (March 2022).
The two ICMR workflows differ on the continuation phase (RHZ vs RHE); shown side by side.
unverifiedSections: British Medical Research Council (MRC) grading and Glasgow Coma Scale cut-offs are not in the opened STW.
Timing of antiretroviral therapy in HIV co-infection is not given in the opened sources; follow the national HIV programme and an HIV specialist.
Management of hydrocephalus (shunt), hyponatraemia and paradoxical reactions is not detailed in the STW.
CSF numeric thresholds other than cell counts are not given in the STW table; typical adult normal ranges are shown.
Drug cautions and contraindications without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.
US labels (DailyMed) were used where Indian sources give no dose; confirm against the Indian product label (CDSCO) and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Tuberculous meningitis is the most severe form of tuberculosis. Mycobacterium tuberculosis seeds the brain surface and forms a thick basal exudate that strangles cranial nerves and blood vessels and blocks CSF flow, causing cranial nerve palsies, infarcts and hydrocephalus. It usually presents subacutely with fever for 5 days or more, headache, vomiting and altered sensorium (ICMR STW). Outcome depends on starting ATT and steroids early, so treatment is often started on clinical and CSF grounds before microbiological proof; a negative nucleic acid test does not exclude TBM (ICMR STW).
keyMechanisms: Rich foci near the meninges rupture into the subarachnoid space.
Thick basal exudate entraps cranial nerves (especially VI, III) and blocks CSF flow (hydrocephalus).
Vasculitis of penetrating arteries causes infarcts and hemiparesis.
Inflammation drives raised intracranial pressure and hyponatraemia (syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, SIADH).

symptoms: Fever for 5 days or more (ICMR STW)
Neck pain and stiffness; weight loss, night sweats (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Papilloedema or focal deficit: computed tomography (CT) before lumbar puncture (ICMR STW)
Worsening headache with vomiting or drowsiness: hydrocephalus or raised pressure (ICMR STW)
New weakness of legs with bladder involvement: myelitis or spinal disease (ICMR STW)
Persistent confusion: hyponatraemia or SIADH (ICMR STW)
precipitants: Active or past TB, previous ATT (ICMR STW)
Contact with a TB patient (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Acute onset; CSF cells in thousands, neutrophils, very low sugar; Gram stain and culture (ICMR STW).
Often HIV; India ink, cryptococcal antigen positive (ICMR STW).
CSF 50–500 lymphocytes, normal sugar; viral PCR (ICMR STW).
Imaging shows cysts or ring lesions; CSF less inflammatory.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Fever 5 days or more with headache, vomiting, altered sensorium, cranial nerve palsy, weakness, seizures or neck stiffness — do not delay CSF examination.
Cells usually under 500, lymphocytic (neutrophilic in some acute cases); high protein; low sugar; acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear and culture; nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT).
Intensive phase 2 months RHZE or RHZS; continuation at least 10 months RHZ; may be extended.
Dexamethasone 0.4 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 divided doses while in hospital; oral taper to a total of 8–12 weeks.

ruleIn.testName: CSF cell count, protein and sugar (with blood sugar)
ruleIn.normalValue: White cells 0–5/µL; protein 15–45 mg/dL; CSF sugar about two-thirds of blood sugar
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Cells usually under 500, lymphocytic; high protein; low sugar
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Pattern supports TBM and guides empirical ATT (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Suspect and investigate
actions: Refer to a centre with lumbar puncture and CT (ICMR STW).
CT head first if papilloedema or focal deficit; then lumbar puncture (ICMR STW).
Send CSF promptly; if delayed, refrigerate and transport on ice (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Start treatment
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as TBM is likely
actions: Start ATT on clinical and CSF grounds; do not wait for NAAT (ICMR STW).
Pyridoxine 10 mg daily with isoniazid (NTEP STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: Watch for worsening headache or drowsiness (hydrocephalus), vision loss, new weakness, seizures, confusion (hyponatraemia) (ICMR STW).
Monitor liver function for drug toxicity (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Discharge and follow-up
actions: Oral steroid taper to complete 8–12 weeks (ICMR STW).
Review monthly for at least the first 3 months, then at longer intervals until treatment ends (ICMR STW).
Notify to NTEP and register for treatment support.

regimens.dose: Weight bands: 25–34 kg 2 tablets; 35–49 kg 3; 50–64 kg 4; 65–75 kg 5; over 75 kg 6 (each 4-FDC: H 75 mg, R 150 mg, Z 400 mg, E 275 mg)
adjustments: Paediatric: Children: use paediatric TBM regimen.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Ethambutol is renally cleared: reduce frequency in kidney impairment; specialist advice.
CLD: Monitor liver function; see ATT-induced hepatitis topic if transaminases rise.

medicationPlan.note: ATT phases, steroids and complications from the ICMR Adult TBM STW (March 2022); weight bands, mg/kg doses, streptomycin and pyridoxine from the ICMR NTEP drug-sensitive TB STW (March 2022). The TBM STW gives RHZ for continuation (ethambutol omitted for toxicity, sent to NTEP); the NTEP STW gives RHE. Drug-resistant TBM needs specialist care. Not clinically reviewed.

keyPoints: Fever 5 days or more with headache and confusion: do a lumbar puncture.
Negative NAAT does not rule out TBM.
2 months intensive, at least 10 months continuation.
pitfalls: Waiting for microbiological proof before treating.
Missing hydrocephalus in a patient getting drowsier.
Ethambutol without vision monitoring in an unconscious patient.

patientEducation: Take ATT every day for the full course (about a year).
Report yellow eyes, vomiting, blurred vision or numb feet.
Steroids must be tapered, not stopped suddenly.
lifestyleAndDiet: Good nutrition; NTEP nutritional support where available
dischargeCriteria: Improving consciousness and no new deficits
Tolerating oral ATT and steroid taper
